questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Mars looks red because its dust has a lot of rusty iron in it.

questions.q: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.fact: Jupiter is so big that more than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and also the smallest planet.

questions.q: What do we call a scientist who studies stars and planets?
questions.fact: Astronomers use telescopes and math to learn about stars, planets, and galaxies.

questions.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon in 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission.

questions.q: Who was the first person to travel into space?
questions.fact: Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union orbited Earth in 1961.

questions.q: Which planet is famous for its big, bright rings?
questions.fact: Saturn's rings are made of countless chunks of ice and rock.

questions.q: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
questions.fact: Our solar system is one small part of the Milky Way, a galaxy with billions of stars.

questions.q: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
questions.fact: Venus has thick clouds that trap heat, so it is even hotter than Mercury.

questions.q: How long does it take Earth to travel once around the Sun?
questions.fact: Earth takes about 365 days to orbit the Sun. That trip is what we call a year.

questions.q: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.fact: Earth spins once about every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day.

questions.q: What is a shooting star really?
questions.fact: A shooting star is a meteor, a bit of space rock that glows as it burns up in Earth's air.

questions.q: What force keeps the planets moving around the Sun?
questions.fact: The Sun's gravity pulls on the planets and keeps them in their orbits.

questions.q: Which planet spins tipped over on its side?
questions.fact: Uranus is tilted so much that it spins almost on its side as it orbits the Sun.

questions.q: What was the name of the first satellite launched into space in 1957?
questions.fact: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in 1957, which started the space age.

questions.q: Which famous space telescope was launched into orbit in 1990?
questions.fact: The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth and has taken amazing pictures of faraway galaxies.

questions.q: What does a light-year measure?
questions.fact: A light-year is how far light travels in one year, about 9.5 trillion kilometers.

questions.q: Which planet has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot?
questions.fact: The Great Red Spot is a huge storm on Jupiter that has been seen for more than 150 years.

questions.q: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.fact: There are eight planets. In 2006, Pluto was moved into a group called dwarf planets.

questions.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.fact: Neptune is the eighth planet from the Sun. It is cold, windy, and deep blue.

questions.q: What is the largest animal on Earth today?
questions.fact: A blue whale can grow to about 30 meters long, longer than two school buses.

questions.q: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.fact: Cheetahs can run over 100 km per hour, but only for short sprints.

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.fact: Spiders have eight legs. Insects have six, so spiders are not insects.

questions.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.fact: A joey is born tiny and keeps growing safely inside its mother's pouch.

questions.q: What is a group of lions called?
questions.fact: A pride is a family group of lions that lives and hunts together.

questions.q: Which bird is able to fly backward?
questions.fact: Hummingbirds beat their wings so fast they can hover in place and even fly backward.

questions.q: What is the tallest animal in the world?
questions.fact: Giraffes can be over 5 meters tall, and their long necks help them reach treetop leaves.

questions.q: Which mammal can truly fly, not just glide?
questions.fact: Bats are the only mammals that can really fly. Flying squirrels can only glide.

questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.fact: An octopus has three hearts, and its blood is blue.

questions.q: What does a caterpillar turn into when it grows up?
questions.fact: Inside a chrysalis or cocoon, a caterpillar completely changes its body.

questions.q: What is the largest bird in the world?
questions.fact: Ostriches cannot fly, but they run very fast and lay the biggest eggs of any living bird.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a Komodo dragon?
questions.fact: The Komodo dragon is the largest living lizard. It lives on a few islands in Indonesia.

questions.q: What is a young frog that lives in water and has a tail called?
questions.fact: Tadpoles breathe with gills, then grow legs and lungs as they turn into frogs.

questions.q: What food do giant pandas mostly eat?
questions.fact: Giant pandas spend many hours every day munching on bamboo.

questions.q: What type of animal is a dolphin?
questions.fact: Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole and feed their babies milk, like other mammals.

questions.q: Which sea animal has no brain, no heart, and no bones?
questions.fact: Jellyfish have no brain, heart, or bones. Their bodies are mostly water.

questions.q: How do honeybees show other bees where to find flowers?
questions.fact: Honeybees do a waggle dance that shows other bees which way to go and how far.

questions.q: Which animal spends most of its life hanging upside down in trees?
questions.fact: Sloths move so slowly that tiny green algae can grow in their fur.

questions.q: What do you call an animal that eats only plants?
questions.fact: Herbivores like cows, deer, and rabbits eat plants. Carnivores eat meat.

questions.q: What is the largest fish in the ocean?
questions.fact: The whale shark is a gentle giant that eats tiny floating plankton.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.fact: Each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.q: Which gas do plants take in from the air to make food?
questions.fact: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen, which we breathe.

questions.q: At what temperature does water freeze on the Celsius scale?
questions.fact: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius, which is the same as 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.q: What are the three states of matter we see in everyday life?
questions.fact: Ice, water, and steam are the same stuff in three different states.

questions.q: Which scientist came up with the theory of relativity?
questions.fact: Albert Einstein's theory of relativity changed how we understand space, time, and gravity.

questions.q: What is the hardest natural material on Earth?
questions.fact: Diamonds are made of carbon atoms packed together very tightly.

questions.q: What is the center of an atom called?
questions.fact: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons, and electrons move around it.

questions.q: What do solar panels use to make electricity?
questions.fact: Solar panels turn the energy in sunlight straight into electricity.

questions.q: What color do you get by mixing blue and yellow paint?
questions.fact: Blue and yellow are primary colors in paint, and together they make green.

questions.q: Which of these materials does a magnet pull on?
questions.fact: Magnets attract iron and a few other metals, like nickel and cobalt.

questions.q: Which gas makes up most of the air we breathe?
questions.fact: About 78 percent of air is nitrogen. Only about 21 percent is oxygen.

questions.q: What is the process plants use to make food from sunlight?
questions.fact: In photosynthesis, plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Au?
questions.fact: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

questions.q: Which of these travels the fastest?
questions.fact: Light is so much faster than sound that you see lightning before you hear thunder.

questions.q: Which scientist wrote the three laws of motion?
questions.fact: Isaac Newton described how forces make things move, stop, and change direction.

questions.q: Which scientist won Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry?
questions.fact: Marie Curie studied radioactivity and was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes.

questions.q: What do we call a substance made of only one kind of atom?
questions.fact: Elements like gold, oxygen, and carbon are listed on the periodic table.

questions.q: What is the pH of pure water?
questions.fact: A pH of 7 is neutral. Lower numbers are acids and higher numbers are bases.

questions.q: What is it called when liquid water turns into vapor?
questions.fact: Puddles dry up after rain because the water evaporates into the air.

questions.q: Why can't sound travel through outer space?
choices: There is no air to carry it
questions.fact: Sound needs air, water, or something solid to travel through. Space is almost empty.

questions.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.fact: The Pacific Ocean is so big that all of Earth's land could fit inside it.

questions.q: What is the outermost layer of Earth called?
questions.fact: The crust is the thin, rocky layer we live on. It is thinnest under the oceans.

questions.q: What is Earth's inner core mostly made of?
questions.fact: Earth's inner core is a very hot, solid ball made mostly of iron and nickel.

questions.q: What is melted rock called while it is still underground?
questions.fact: Melted rock is called magma underground and lava once it comes out of a volcano.

questions.q: What instrument records the shaking from earthquakes?
questions.fact: A seismometer measures how the ground moves during an earthquake.

questions.q: Which type of rock forms when lava or magma cools and hardens?
questions.fact: Igneous rocks, like granite and basalt, form from melted rock that cooled.

questions.q: Which layer high in the sky blocks a lot of the Sun's harmful rays?
questions.fact: The ozone layer soaks up much of the Sun's ultraviolet light, which can burn skin.

questions.q: What are the giant moving pieces of Earth's crust called?
questions.fact: Earth's crust is broken into plates that slowly move a few centimeters each year.

questions.q: What was the name of the supercontinent that formed millions of years ago?
questions.fact: About 300 million years ago, most of Earth's land was joined together as Pangaea.

questions.q: In the water cycle, what is rain or snow falling from clouds called?
questions.fact: Precipitation is any water that falls from clouds, like rain, snow, sleet, or hail.

questions.q: Which tall cloud type often brings thunderstorms?
questions.fact: Cumulonimbus clouds can tower many kilometers high and bring lightning and heavy rain.

questions.q: What do we call a scientist who studies rocks and the Earth?
questions.fact: Geologists study rocks, volcanoes, and earthquakes to learn Earth's history.

questions.q: What is a huge, slow-moving river of ice called?
questions.fact: Glaciers form when snow piles up for many years and gets squeezed into ice.

questions.q: What mainly causes the ocean tides?
questions.fact: The Moon's gravity pulls on the oceans, making the water rise and fall. The Sun helps a little too.

questions.q: What do we call a spot where hot water and steam shoot out of the ground?
questions.fact: Old Faithful in Yellowstone National Park is one of the most famous geysers.

questions.q: Which layer of the atmosphere do we live in?
questions.fact: The troposphere is the lowest layer of air, and almost all weather happens there.

questions.q: What do we call the remains of ancient living things preserved in rock?
questions.fact: Fossils of bones, shells, and footprints help scientists learn about life long ago.

questions.q: Which is the coldest continent on Earth?
questions.fact: Antarctica is covered by a huge sheet of ice and is the coldest place on Earth.

questions.q: What is a hurricane called in the western Pacific Ocean?
questions.fact: Hurricanes, typhoons, and cyclones are the same kind of storm with different names by region.

questions.q: Which two things are needed to make a rainbow?
questions.fact: Raindrops bend sunlight and split it into its colors, making a rainbow.

questions.q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.fact: Your skin covers your whole body and protects you from germs, heat, and cold.

questions.q: How many bones does an adult human have?
questions.fact: Babies are born with more bones, but some of them join together as they grow.

questions.q: Which organ pumps blood around your body?
questions.fact: Your heart is a strong muscle that beats about 100,000 times a day.

questions.q: Where in your body is the smallest bone found?
questions.fact: The stapes, a tiny bone in your middle ear, is about the size of a grain of rice.

questions.q: What is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.fact: The thigh bone, called the femur, is the longest and strongest bone in your body.

questions.q: Which gas do your lungs take from the air for your body to use?
questions.fact: Your blood carries oxygen from your lungs to every part of your body.

questions.q: Which blood cells help fight germs?
questions.fact: White blood cells find and attack germs to help keep you from getting sick.

questions.q: What is the colored part of your eye called?
questions.fact: The iris is a ring of muscle that makes the pupil bigger or smaller to control light.

questions.q: How many baby teeth do most kids have?
questions.fact: Most kids have 20 baby teeth, which are later replaced by adult teeth.

questions.q: Which organs clean your blood and make urine?
questions.fact: You have two kidneys, and they filter waste out of your blood all day long.

questions.q: Which tube carries food from your mouth to your stomach?
questions.fact: Muscles in the esophagus squeeze food down to your stomach, even if you are upside down.

questions.q: Which vitamin does your skin make when sunlight hits it?
questions.fact: Vitamin D helps your body use calcium to build strong bones.

questions.q: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.fact: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, and veins bring it back.

questions.q: What connects your muscles to your bones?
questions.fact: Tendons attach muscles to bones, while ligaments connect bones to other bones.

questions.q: What is the hard white outer layer of your teeth called?
questions.fact: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body.

questions.q: Which bones protect your brain?
questions.fact: Your skull is made of several bones joined tightly together to guard your brain.

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.fact: The heart has two upper chambers called atria and two lower chambers called ventricles.

questions.q: Which body system includes your brain, spinal cord, and nerves?
questions.fact: Your nervous system sends messages between your brain and the rest of your body.

questions.q: Where does most digestion of food happen?
questions.fact: Most food is broken down and soaked into your blood in the small intestine.

questions.q: Which protein in red blood cells carries oxygen?
questions.fact: Hemoglobin contains iron, and it is what makes blood red.

questions.q: Which ancient people built the pyramids of Giza?
questions.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built more than 4,000 years ago as a tomb for a pharaoh.

questions.q: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.fact: George Washington became the first president in 1789.

questions.q: In what year did Christopher Columbus first reach the Americas?
questions.fact: Columbus sailed from Spain in 1492 with three ships.

questions.q: Which famous ship sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
questions.fact: The Titanic sank on its very first voyage, across the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.q: Who was the main writer of the Declaration of Independence?
questions.fact: Thomas Jefferson wrote most of the Declaration, which was adopted in 1776.

questions.q: What is the name of the long wall built across northern China?
questions.fact: The Great Wall was built and rebuilt over many centuries to protect China from invaders.

questions.q: In what year did World War II end?
questions.fact: World War II lasted from 1939 to 1945 and involved countries all over the world.

questions.q: Which famous queen of Egypt was allied with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony?
questions.fact: Cleopatra ruled until 30 BC. After her death, Egypt became part of the Roman Empire.

questions.q: Which Roman city was buried when Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD 79?
questions.fact: Ash from the volcano buried Pompeii, and it stayed hidden for over 1,500 years.

questions.q: Who built a printing press with movable type in Europe around 1440?
questions.fact: Gutenberg's press made books much faster and cheaper to produce.

questions.q: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.fact: The wall split Berlin from 1961 to 1989. Germany was reunited in 1990.

questions.q: Who gave the famous "I Have a Dream" speech in 1963?
questions.fact: Martin Luther King Jr. gave the speech in Washington, D.C., calling for equal rights.

questions.q: Whose expedition was the first to sail all the way around the world?
questions.fact: Magellan died during the voyage, but his crew finished the trip around the world in 1522.

questions.q: In which country did the ancient Olympic Games begin?
questions.fact: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia, Greece, in honor of the god Zeus.

questions.q: Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.fact: Amelia Earhart flew alone across the Atlantic in 1932.

questions.q: Which brothers made the first powered airplane flight in 1903?
questions.fact: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew their plane at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

questions.q: What did the ancient Romans build to carry water into their cities?
questions.fact: Roman aqueducts used gentle slopes so gravity could carry water many kilometers.

questions.q: Which document, signed in 1215, limited the power of the English king?
questions.fact: King John agreed to the Magna Carta, which said even the king had to follow the law.

questions.q: What were the skilled warriors of old Japan called?
questions.fact: Samurai were Japanese warriors who followed a strict code of honor.

questions.q: Which Italian artist painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.fact: Leonardo da Vinci was also an inventor who sketched ideas for flying machines.

questions.q: What is the largest continent by area?
questions.fact: Asia is the biggest continent and covers about a third of Earth's land.

questions.q: What is the capital city of France?
questions.fact: Paris is home to the Eiffel Tower, which was finished in 1889.

questions.q: Which country is home to the Great Barrier Reef?
questions.fact: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, off northeast Australia.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Japan?
questions.fact: Tokyo is Japan's capital. Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

questions.q: What is the tallest mountain above sea level?
questions.fact: Mount Everest is in the Himalayas, on the border of Nepal and China.

questions.q: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.fact: The Sahara covers much of North Africa and is about as big as the United States.

questions.q: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.fact: Italy sticks out into the Mediterranean Sea in the shape of a tall boot.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Canada?
questions.fact: Many people guess Toronto, but Ottawa is Canada's capital.

questions.q: Which river flows through London?
questions.fact: The River Thames runs through the middle of London. The Seine flows through Paris.

questions.q: What is the smallest country in the world?
questions.fact: Vatican City is a tiny country inside the city of Rome, Italy.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.fact: Sydney is the biggest city, but Canberra was chosen to be Australia's capital.

questions.q: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
questions.fact: The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean on Earth.

questions.q: What is the imaginary line around the middle of Earth called?
questions.fact: The equator divides Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

questions.q: Which mountain range runs down the west side of South America?
questions.fact: The Andes are the longest mountain range on land in the world.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Egypt?
questions.fact: Cairo sits beside the Nile River, not far from the pyramids of Giza.

questions.q: In which city is the Statue of Liberty?
questions.fact: France gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States, and it was dedicated in 1886.

questions.q: In which country is the ancient city of Machu Picchu?
questions.fact: Machu Picchu is an Inca city built high in the mountains of Peru.

questions.q: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
questions.fact: Russia is so wide that it stretches across two continents, Europe and Asia.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Brazil?
questions.fact: Brasilia was built from scratch and became Brazil's capital in 1960.

questions.q: Which body of water is so salty that people float easily in it?
questions.fact: The Dead Sea is so salty that fish cannot live in it, but swimmers bob like corks.

questions.q: How many players does a soccer team have on the field at once?
questions.fact: Each soccer team has 11 players on the field, including the goalkeeper.

questions.q: In which sport can a player score with a slam dunk?
questions.fact: A slam dunk is when a player jumps up and pushes the ball down through the hoop.

questions.q: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football?
questions.fact: A touchdown is worth 6 points, and the team can then try for 1 or 2 extra points.

questions.q: In tennis, what is a score of zero called?
questions.fact: In tennis, love means zero, so a score of 15 to 0 is called fifteen love.

questions.q: How often are the Summer Olympic Games usually held?
questions.fact: The Summer and Winter Olympics each happen every four years, two years apart.

questions.q: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.fact: The five linked rings stand for the parts of the world coming together at the Games.

questions.q: In baseball, how many strikes does it take to strike out?
questions.fact: Three strikes and the batter is out. Four balls let the batter walk to first base.

questions.q: How many holes are in a standard round of golf?
questions.fact: Golfers try to finish all 18 holes using as few strokes as possible.

questions.q: Which sport is played on ice with sticks and a puck?
questions.fact: A hockey puck is a hard rubber disk that can fly across the ice very fast.

questions.q: About how long is a marathon race?
questions.fact: A marathon is 42.195 kilometers, or about 26.2 miles.

questions.q: In which sport do you roll a ball to knock down ten pins?
questions.fact: Knocking down all ten pins with your first ball is called a strike.

questions.q: How many players from one team are on a basketball court at once?
questions.fact: Each basketball team has five players on the court at a time.

questions.q: In which country did the sport of judo begin?
questions.fact: Judo was created in Japan in 1882 by a teacher named Jigoro Kano.

questions.q: In soccer, which player is allowed to use their hands?
questions.fact: Only the goalkeeper may use their hands, and only inside their own penalty area.

questions.q: What is it called when one player scores three goals in one game?
questions.fact: The term hat trick started in cricket and is now used in soccer and hockey too.

questions.q: Which sport uses rackets and a feathered shuttlecock?
questions.fact: A badminton shuttlecock is also called a birdie.

questions.q: Which swimming stroke is done lying on your back?
questions.fact: Backstroke is the only Olympic swimming race that starts in the water.

questions.q: What kind of race is the Tour de France?
questions.fact: The Tour de France is a bike race that lasts about three weeks. It began in 1903.

questions.q: What do runners in a relay race pass to each other?
questions.fact: In a relay, each runner must hand the baton to the next runner inside a set zone.

questions.q: Which sport involves sliding stones across ice while teammates sweep?
questions.fact: In curling, sweeping the ice helps the stone slide farther and straighter.

questions.q: What does CPU stand for?
questions.fact: The CPU is the part of a computer that follows instructions and does calculations.

questions.q: Who received the first patent for the telephone in 1876?
questions.fact: Bell's first words on the phone were to his assistant, Mr. Watson.

questions.q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.fact: Tim Berners-Lee came up with the web in 1989 while working at CERN in Europe.

questions.q: What number system do computers use, made of only 0s and 1s?
questions.fact: Computers store everything, from games to photos, as long lines of 0s and 1s.

questions.q: What does GPS stand for?
questions.fact: GPS uses signals from satellites to work out exactly where you are.

questions.q: Which company makes the iPad?
questions.fact: Apple released the very first iPad in 2010.

questions.q: Which inventor created the phonograph, a machine that recorded sound?
questions.fact: Thomas Edison invented the phonograph in 1877 and recorded himself saying a nursery rhyme.

questions.q: What does Wi-Fi let devices do?
questions.fact: Wi-Fi uses radio waves to link devices to the internet without cables.

questions.q: Which early electronic computer, finished in 1945, filled an entire room?
questions.fact: ENIAC weighed about 27 tons and used thousands of glowing vacuum tubes.

questions.q: What is a bug in computer programming?
questions.fact: Finding and fixing mistakes in code is called debugging.

questions.q: Which coding language for kids uses colorful blocks you snap together?
questions.fact: Scratch was created at MIT so anyone could learn to code by building games and stories.

questions.q: What is the name for software made to harm a computer?
questions.fact: Malware is short for malicious software. Viruses are one kind of malware.

questions.q: Which British scientist helped crack secret codes in World War II?
questions.fact: Alan Turing is often called the father of computer science.

questions.q: Who is often called the first computer programmer?
questions.fact: In the 1840s, Ada Lovelace wrote steps for a machine designed by Charles Babbage.

questions.q: What does USB stand for?
questions.fact: USB is a standard way to plug devices into computers and charge them.

questions.q: Which device turns your voice into an electrical signal?
questions.fact: A microphone changes sound into electricity. A speaker does the opposite.

questions.q: What kind of screen reacts when you tap it with your finger?
questions.fact: Touchscreens on tablets sense the tiny electric charge in your fingertip.

questions.q: What does AI stand for?
questions.fact: Artificial intelligence means computer programs that can learn and solve problems.

questions.q: Which company develops the Android operating system?
questions.fact: Android runs on phones and tablets from many different brands.

questions.q: What is HTML used to create?
questions.fact: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It tells a browser how to show a page.

questions.q: What is guacamole mainly made from?
questions.fact: Guacamole comes from Mexico and is made by mashing ripe avocados.

questions.q: Which country is famous for creating pizza?
questions.fact: Modern pizza comes from the city of Naples in Italy.

questions.q: Raisins are made by drying which fruit?
questions.fact: Raisins are grapes that have been dried. Dried plums are called prunes.

questions.q: A peanut is not a true nut. What is it?
questions.fact: Peanuts are legumes, like beans and peas, and they grow underground.

questions.q: Which country is famous for sushi?
questions.fact: Sushi is a Japanese dish made with rice flavored with vinegar, often with fish or vegetables.

questions.q: Which food is made by churning cream?
questions.fact: Shaking or stirring cream for a long time makes the fat clump together into butter.

questions.q: Popcorn is made from which grain?
questions.fact: Each popcorn kernel has a little water inside that turns to steam and makes it pop.

questions.q: Which fruit has its seeds on the outside?
questions.fact: The tiny dots on a strawberry's skin each hold a seed.

questions.q: What sweet food do bees make from flower nectar?
questions.fact: Bees store honey in wax honeycombs to feed their hive.

questions.q: Where does maple syrup come from?
questions.fact: Maple syrup is made by boiling down sap from maple trees until it gets thick and sweet.

questions.q: What is tofu made from?
questions.fact: Tofu is made by curdling soy milk and pressing it into blocks.

questions.q: Which vegetable often makes people cry when they cut it?
questions.fact: Cutting an onion releases a gas that stings your eyes and makes them water.

questions.q: Chocolate is made from the beans of which plant?
questions.fact: Cacao beans grow in pods on cacao trees and are roasted to make chocolate.

questions.q: Which spice comes from the inner bark of a tree?
questions.fact: Cinnamon bark curls up into rolls called sticks as it dries.

questions.q: Which country does the rice dish paella come from?
questions.fact: Paella comes from Valencia in Spain and is cooked in a wide, shallow pan.

questions.q: What makes bread dough rise and get fluffy?
questions.fact: Yeast is a tiny living fungus that makes gas bubbles in the dough.

questions.q: What is the main ingredient in hummus?
questions.fact: Hummus is made by blending chickpeas with sesame paste, lemon juice, and garlic.

questions.q: Which vitamin are oranges famous for?
questions.fact: Vitamin C helps your body heal cuts and fight off sickness.

questions.q: Botanists say a tomato is which part of a plant?
questions.fact: Tomatoes grow from flowers and hold seeds, so scientists call them fruits.

questions.q: Most dried pasta is made from which grain?
questions.fact: Most dried pasta is made from durum wheat flour and water.

questions.q: What is a baby cat called?
questions.fact: Kittens are born with their eyes closed and open them after about one to two weeks.

questions.q: What is a baby goat called?
questions.fact: Baby goats can stand and walk within minutes of being born.

questions.q: What is a baby horse called?
questions.fact: A young female horse is called a filly and a young male is called a colt.

questions.q: What is a baby swan called?
questions.fact: Cygnets are usually gray or brown, not white like their parents.

questions.q: What is a baby goose called?
questions.fact: Goslings can swim within a day or so of hatching.

questions.q: What is a baby owl called?
questions.fact: Owlets are covered in fluffy down feathers before their adult feathers grow in.

questions.q: What is a baby deer called?
questions.fact: Many fawns have white spots that help them hide in dappled forest light.

questions.q: What is a baby bear called?
questions.fact: Black bear cubs are about the size of a squirrel when they are born.

questions.q: What is a baby whale called?
questions.fact: A newborn blue whale calf can weigh more than 2,500 kilograms.

questions.q: What is a baby fox called?
questions.fact: Fox kits are born in an underground den.

questions.q: What is a baby seal called?
questions.fact: Some seal pups are born with fluffy white fur.

questions.q: What is a baby eel called?
questions.fact: Young eels are see-through when they are small and are called glass eels.

questions.q: What is a group of crows called?
questions.fact: Crows are very smart and can recognize individual human faces.

questions.q: What is a group of owls called?
questions.fact: The name may come from an old story that described owls as wise.

questions.q: What is a group of whales or dolphins called?
questions.fact: Some dolphin pods join together to make superpods of more than a thousand animals.

questions.q: What is a group of fish swimming together called?
questions.fact: Swimming in a school helps fish confuse predators.

questions.q: What is a group of wolves called?
questions.fact: A wolf pack is usually a family made of parents and their young.

questions.q: What is a group of geese on the ground called?
questions.fact: Flying geese in a V shape are often called a skein.

questions.q: What is a group of monkeys called?
questions.fact: Some monkey troops have more than a hundred members.

questions.q: What is a group of flamingos called?
questions.fact: Flamingos often stand on one leg, even while sleeping.

questions.q: What is a group of ants called?
questions.fact: Some ant colonies have millions of ants working together.

questions.q: What is a group of cows called?
questions.fact: Cows in a herd often have best friends and get stressed when separated.

questions.q: What is the fastest bird in a dive?
questions.fact: A diving peregrine falcon can go faster than 320 kilometers per hour.

questions.q: What is the fastest fish in the sea?
questions.fact: Sailfish are often said to reach speeds of over 100 kilometers per hour in short bursts.

questions.q: Which is the largest living land animal?
questions.fact: A big male African elephant can weigh about 6,000 kilograms or more.

questions.q: Which animal has the longest pregnancy of any mammal?
questions.fact: An elephant mother is pregnant for about 22 months.

questions.q: What is an elephant's trunk?
choices: Its nose joined with its upper lip
questions.fact: An elephant's trunk has tens of thousands of muscles.

questions.q: What are an elephant's tusks?
questions.fact: Elephant tusks are made of ivory and keep growing all their lives.

questions.q: How can you tell an African elephant from an Asian elephant?
choices: African elephants have much bigger ears
questions.fact: An African elephant's big ears are shaped a bit like the continent of Africa.

questions.q: Why do elephants flap their big ears?
questions.fact: Blood flowing through their thin ears loses heat when the ears flap.

questions.q: Which animal is the largest living cat?
questions.fact: Siberian tigers, also called Amur tigers, are the biggest of all.

questions.q: Which big cat lives in groups called prides?
questions.fact: Lions are the only truly social big cats.

questions.q: In a lion pride, who does most of the hunting?
questions.fact: Lionesses often hunt together as a team.

questions.q: Which big cat is a great swimmer and often hunts in water?
questions.fact: Unlike most cats, tigers usually enjoy water.

questions.q: What are a tiger's stripes like?
choices: All tigers have the same pattern
Stripes are only on the fur, not the skin
Tigers have spots under their stripes
questions.fact: A tiger's skin is striped too, not just its fur.

questions.q: Which big cat lives high in the mountains of Central Asia?
questions.fact: Snow leopards use their long, thick tails like a scarf to keep warm.

questions.q: Which big cat lives mostly in Central and South America?
questions.fact: Jaguars have one of the strongest bites of all big cats.

questions.q: How can you tell a jaguar's spots from a leopard's?
choices: Jaguar spots often have small dots inside
questions.fact: The rings of spots on both cats are called rosettes.

questions.q: Which cat cannot roar but can purr?
questions.fact: Cheetahs chirp, purr and even make bird-like calls.

questions.q: Why do cheetahs have black lines running from their eyes?
choices: They are tear stains from crying
They help cut down glare from the sun
questions.fact: These tear marks may work like the black grease that some athletes wear under their eyes.

questions.q: What is the largest member of the dog family?
questions.fact: Gray wolves can weigh more than 60 kilograms.

questions.q: Which wild dog lives in Australia?
questions.fact: Dingoes have lived in Australia for thousands of years.

questions.q: Which animal is known for laughing sounds?
questions.fact: The giggle-like sounds help hyenas tell each other who is around and how they feel.

questions.q: What is a zebra's skin color underneath its stripes?
questions.fact: Scientists think the stripes may help keep biting flies away.

questions.q: Which large flightless bird lives only in Australia?
questions.fact: Emus are the second tallest birds in the world after ostriches.

questions.q: Which bird lays the largest eggs?
questions.fact: An ostrich egg weighs about as much as two dozen chicken eggs.

questions.q: Which country is the kiwi bird from?
questions.fact: The kiwi cannot fly and has nostrils at the tip of its long beak.

questions.q: Which bird can turn its head about three quarters of the way around?
questions.fact: Owls cannot move their eyes, so they turn their heads instead.

questions.q: Which bird is the national bird of the United States?
questions.fact: Bald eagles are not actually bald, their heads are covered in white feathers.

questions.q: What do bald eagles mainly eat?
questions.fact: Bald eagles sometimes steal fish from other birds, like ospreys.

questions.q: What makes flamingos pink?
questions.fact: Flamingos eat tiny shrimp and algae full of pink color, and without it their feathers turn pale.

questions.q: Which bird is famous for copying human speech?
questions.fact: An African gray parrot named Alex learned more than 100 words.

questions.q: Which bird has the longest wingspan of any living bird?
questions.fact: A wandering albatross can have wings over 3 meters from tip to tip.

questions.q: Which bird is the smallest in the world?
questions.fact: The bee hummingbird from Cuba is only about 5 centimeters long.

questions.q: How fast can a hummingbird's wings beat?
questions.fact: Some small hummingbirds beat their wings around 80 times a second.

questions.q: Which bird has a huge, colorful bill and lives in South American rainforests?
questions.fact: A toucan's bill looks heavy but is light, made of a spongy material.

questions.q: Which bird can hold lots of fish in a stretchy pouch under its bill?
questions.fact: A brown pelican dives headfirst into the water to catch fish.

questions.q: Which seabird with a colorful beak is sometimes called a sea parrot?
questions.fact: Puffins can carry many small fish in their beaks at once.

questions.q: Which bird is famous for its huge, colorful tail feathers?
questions.fact: Only the males, called peacocks, have the big fancy tails, and the females are called peahens.

questions.q: Where do most penguins live?
questions.fact: No penguins live in the wild at the North Pole.

questions.q: Which is the largest kind of penguin?
questions.fact: Emperor penguins can stand more than 1 meter tall.

questions.q: Which parent keeps an emperor penguin egg warm through the Antarctic winter?
questions.fact: The father balances the egg on his feet under a warm fold of skin for about two months.

questions.q: What is the smallest kind of penguin?
questions.fact: Little penguins, also called fairy penguins, are only about 33 centimeters tall.

questions.q: Which bird builds the biggest nests?
questions.fact: One bald eagle nest in Florida was estimated to weigh more than 2 tons.

questions.q: Which bird can stay in the air for about 10 months without landing?
questions.fact: Common swifts even eat and drink while flying.

questions.q: Which bird migrates the farthest each year?
questions.fact: Arctic terns fly from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year.

questions.q: What do we call it when birds lose old feathers and grow new ones?
questions.fact: Most birds molt at least once a year.

questions.q: Which bird uses tools like twigs to pull insects out of holes?
questions.fact: These crows even bend and shape their tools.

questions.q: Which bird pecks holes in trees to find insects?
questions.fact: Woodpeckers can peck around 20 times every second.

questions.q: Which bird is a symbol of peace?
questions.fact: Doves and pigeons belong to the same bird family.

questions.q: Which bird hoots and hunts mostly at night?
questions.fact: Owls have special soft feathers that let them fly almost silently.

questions.q: Which mammal lays eggs and has a bill like a duck?
questions.fact: Platypuses use their bills to sense tiny electric signals from prey underwater.

questions.q: Besides the platypus, which other mammal lays eggs?
questions.fact: Egg-laying mammals are called monotremes.

questions.q: Where does a mother kangaroo carry her baby?
questions.fact: Animals with pouches are called marsupials.

questions.q: Which animal from Australia sleeps up to 20 hours a day and eats eucalyptus leaves?
questions.fact: Eucalyptus leaves give koalas little energy, so they rest a lot.

questions.q: Is a koala a bear?
questions.fact: Koala babies, like kangaroo babies, are called joeys.

questions.q: Which Australian animal makes poop shaped like cubes?
questions.fact: Wombats leave their cube-shaped poop on rocks and logs to mark their territory.

questions.q: Which marsupial from Tasmania is known for its loud screeches?
questions.fact: Tasmanian devils have one of the strongest bites for their size of any mammal.

questions.q: Which small Australian marsupial is famous for looking like it is smiling?
questions.fact: Quokkas live mostly on Rottnest Island near Perth.

questions.q: Which is the only marsupial native to the United States and Canada?
questions.fact: When scared, an opossum may play dead, flopping over and lying very still.

questions.q: Which animal sprays a bad smell to defend itself?
questions.fact: A skunk can spray its smelly liquid about 3 meters.

questions.q: Which animal has a hard shell made of bony plates and can sometimes roll into a ball?
questions.fact: Only the three-banded armadillo can roll into a complete ball.

questions.q: Which animal is covered in sharp quills?
questions.fact: Porcupines cannot shoot their quills, but the quills come off easily when touched.

questions.q: Which animal builds dams across streams?
questions.fact: Beavers' front teeth never stop growing, and they are orange because of iron.

questions.q: Which animal holds hands with others while sleeping so they don't drift apart?
questions.fact: Sea otters also wrap themselves in seaweed to stay in place.

questions.q: Which animal uses rocks as tools to crack open shellfish?
questions.fact: Sea otters even keep a favorite rock in a pouch of skin under their arm.

questions.q: Which animal has long tusks and uses them to pull itself onto ice?
questions.fact: Both male and female walruses have tusks.

questions.q: Which whale has a long spiral tusk that makes it look like a unicorn?
questions.fact: A narwhal's tusk is actually a long tooth that grows through its lip.

questions.q: Which white whale is known as the canary of the sea for its many sounds?
questions.fact: Belugas can change the shape of their bumpy forehead, called a melon.

questions.q: Which whale is famous for its long, beautiful songs?
questions.fact: Male humpbacks sing songs that can last for hours.

questions.q: What is another name for the orca?
questions.fact: Orcas are actually the largest members of the dolphin family.

questions.q: Which whale has the largest brain of any animal?
questions.fact: A sperm whale's brain weighs about 8 kilograms.

questions.q: How do whales breathe?
choices: Through a blowhole on top of their head
questions.fact: The spout you see is warm breath and water spray from the blowhole.

questions.q: What do blue whales mainly eat?
questions.fact: A blue whale can eat several tons of these tiny shrimp-like animals in a day.

questions.q: What do some whales have in their mouths instead of teeth, to strain food from water?
questions.fact: Baleen is made of keratin, the same stuff as your fingernails.

questions.q: How do dolphins find food using sound?
choices: Seeing in the dark with night vision
questions.fact: Dolphins send out clicks and listen for the echoes bouncing back.

questions.q: How do dolphins sleep?
choices: With both eyes closed for 12 hours
With half of their brain at a time
questions.fact: Keeping half the brain awake lets them keep breathing and watch for danger.

questions.q: Which sea mammal is also called a sea cow?
questions.fact: Manatees are plant eaters and their closest land relatives are elephants.

questions.q: How can you tell a sea lion from a true seal?
choices: Seals can walk on all four flippers
questions.fact: Sea lions can also turn their back flippers forward to walk on land.

questions.q: Which shark is the largest predator fish?
questions.fact: The whale shark is bigger, but it eats tiny plankton instead of hunting big prey.

questions.q: What are shark skeletons made of?
questions.fact: Cartilage is the same bendy material in your nose and ears.

questions.q: How many rows of teeth can a shark have?
choices: Many rows, replaced all through its life
Only one row that never changes
questions.fact: Some sharks lose and replace thousands of teeth in their lifetime.

questions.q: Which shark has a head shaped like a wide flat hammer?
questions.fact: The wide head spreads out the eyes and sensors, helping it find prey.

questions.q: Which shark can swim from the ocean far up into fresh water rivers?
questions.fact: Bull sharks have been found far up the Mississippi and Amazon rivers.

questions.q: Which shark lives the longest, possibly hundreds of years?
questions.fact: Scientists estimate that some Greenland sharks may live 270 years or more.

questions.q: Which fish can puff up into a spiky ball?
questions.fact: Many pufferfish contain a strong poison, so most predators leave them alone.

questions.q: Which fish lives safely among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones?
questions.fact: A slimy coating protects clownfish from the anemone's stings.

questions.q: Which fish swims from the ocean back up the river where it hatched to lay eggs?
questions.fact: Salmon may use their sense of smell to find their home stream.

questions.q: Which fish has a glowing lure on its head to attract prey in the deep sea?
questions.fact: The glow comes from bacteria living in the lure.

questions.q: Which fish has both eyes on one side of its head and lies flat on the sea floor?
questions.fact: Baby flounders start with eyes on both sides, and one eye moves over as they grow.

questions.q: In which fish species does the male give birth?
questions.fact: The female puts her eggs into a pouch on the male's belly, and he carries them until they hatch.

questions.q: Which fish can make strong electric shocks?
questions.fact: Despite its name, the electric eel is actually a type of knifefish.

questions.q: Which fish is known for its sharp teeth and lives in South American rivers?
questions.fact: Most piranhas eat a mix of food, including seeds and fruit, and rarely attack people.

questions.q: What do fish use to breathe underwater?
questions.fact: Gills pull oxygen out of the water as it flows over them.

questions.q: Which ocean animal shoots out ink to escape from predators?
questions.fact: The ink cloud confuses predators while the octopus swims away.

questions.q: What color is an octopus's blood?
questions.fact: Octopus blood uses copper to carry oxygen, which makes it blue.

questions.q: How many arms does an octopus have?
questions.fact: Each arm has its own cluster of nerves and can taste what it touches.

questions.q: Which animal can change both the color and texture of its skin in less than a second?
questions.fact: Octopuses have special color cells in their skin that they control with muscles.

questions.q: Which animal has the largest eyes of any animal?
questions.fact: A colossal squid's eye can be about the size of a soccer ball.

questions.q: How many arms does a typical sea star have?
questions.fact: Some sea stars can regrow a lost arm, and a few kinds have many more arms.

questions.q: Is a sea star a fish?
questions.fact: Sea stars have no blood and move water through their bodies instead.

questions.q: Which ocean animal is actually a colony of many tiny animals living together?
questions.fact: Each part of a man o' war is a separate tiny creature, and they cannot live alone.

questions.q: What is a coral reef made from?
choices: Skeletons of tiny animals called coral polyps
questions.fact: Coral reefs cover a tiny part of the ocean floor but are home to about a quarter of all ocean species.

questions.q: Which animal is a hermit crab known for using as a home?
questions.fact: Hermit crabs move into bigger shells as they grow.

questions.q: How many legs does a crab have?
questions.fact: Two of the crab's ten legs are its front claws, called pincers.

questions.q: Which sea turtle is the largest?
questions.fact: Leatherbacks can weigh more than 500 kilograms.

questions.q: Where do sea turtles lay their eggs?
choices: In nests dug on sandy beaches
questions.fact: Many females return to lay eggs on the same beach where they hatched.

questions.q: What decides whether many baby sea turtles hatch as males or females?
questions.fact: Warmer nests mostly produce females and cooler nests mostly produce males.

questions.q: Which reptile can live for more than 150 years?
questions.fact: A giant tortoise named Jonathan, living on the island of Saint Helena, was over 190 years old as of 2025.

questions.q: What is the difference between a tortoise and a turtle?
choices: Tortoises live on land, while many turtles live in water
questions.fact: Tortoises usually have rounded, dome-shaped shells and stumpy legs.

questions.q: Which reptile is the largest living reptile?
questions.fact: Big male saltwater crocodiles can grow longer than 6 meters.

questions.q: How can you tell a crocodile from an alligator?
choices: Crocodiles usually have a narrower, pointed snout
questions.fact: When a crocodile closes its mouth, you can usually still see some of its lower teeth.

questions.q: In which two countries do wild alligators live?
questions.fact: The Chinese alligator is much smaller and is critically endangered.

questions.q: Which lizard can change color and move its eyes in two directions at once?
questions.fact: A chameleon's tongue can be longer than its whole body.

questions.q: Which lizard can walk up walls and even across ceilings?
questions.fact: Geckos have millions of tiny hairs on their toes that stick to surfaces.

questions.q: Which lizard can squirt blood from its eyes to scare away predators?
questions.fact: The blood tastes bad to predators like dogs and coyotes.

questions.q: Why do some lizards drop their tails?
questions.fact: The tail keeps wiggling to distract the predator, and a new tail can grow back.

questions.q: Which venomous lizard lives in the deserts of the southwestern United States and Mexico?
questions.fact: Gila monsters spend most of their lives underground.

questions.q: Which is the longest snake in the world?
questions.fact: Reticulated pythons can grow longer than 6 meters.

questions.q: Which is the heaviest snake in the world?
questions.fact: Green anacondas can weigh more than 90 kilograms, about as much as a grown-up.

questions.q: Which is the longest venomous snake?
questions.fact: King cobras can be more than 5 meters long and mostly eat other snakes.

questions.q: How do snakes smell?
questions.fact: A snake flicks its tongue to collect smells and then presses it to a special organ in its mouth.

questions.q: What does a rattlesnake use its rattle for?
choices: To warn animals to stay away
questions.fact: A new segment is added to the rattle each time the snake sheds its skin.

questions.q: How do snakes grow?
questions.fact: Snakes often shed their skin in one long piece, inside out.

questions.q: How do snakes like pythons and boas kill their prey?
questions.fact: Snakes that squeeze their prey are called constrictors.

questions.q: Do snakes have eyelids?
questions.fact: Instead, a clear scale covers and protects each eye.

questions.q: What are the only animals that have feathers?
questions.fact: Some dinosaurs had feathers too, and birds are their living relatives.

questions.q: Which amphibian can regrow lost legs, and even parts of its heart and brain?
questions.fact: Axolotls are a kind of salamander from lakes near Mexico City.

questions.q: How do frogs drink water?
choices: They soak it up through their skin
questions.fact: Many frogs have a special patch of skin on their belly for soaking up water.

questions.q: What is the difference between a frog and a toad?
choices: Toads usually have dry, bumpy skin and shorter legs
questions.fact: All toads are actually a type of frog.

questions.q: Which brightly colored frog from rainforests has poisonous skin?
questions.fact: Some Indigenous people used the poison on the tips of their blow darts.

questions.q: What does the word amphibian mean?
questions.fact: Most amphibians start life in water and later live partly on land.

questions.q: Which animal group are frogs, toads and salamanders part of?
questions.fact: Amphibians have thin skin that must stay moist.

questions.q: How many legs do insects have?
questions.fact: Insects also have three main body parts: head, thorax and abdomen.

questions.q: Which group of animals do spiders belong to?
questions.fact: Scorpions, ticks and mites are arachnids too.

questions.q: What is the name for an animal with no backbone?
questions.fact: About 97 percent of all animal species are invertebrates.

questions.q: What do caterpillars turn into inside a chrysalis to become butterflies?
choices: They grow wings on the outside first
questions.fact: This complete change of body shape is called metamorphosis.

questions.q: Which butterfly travels thousands of kilometers from Canada to Mexico every year?
questions.fact: Millions of monarchs spend the winter clustered on trees in the mountains of Mexico.

questions.q: What do butterflies taste with?
questions.fact: Butterflies stand on a leaf to taste whether it is good for laying eggs.

questions.q: Which insect makes honey?
questions.fact: A single honeybee makes only about one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole life.

questions.q: Who is the only bee in a hive that lays eggs?
questions.fact: A queen bee can lay up to about 2,000 eggs in a single day.

questions.q: What are male honeybees called?
questions.fact: Drones do not have stingers.

questions.q: What happens to a honeybee after it stings a person?
questions.fact: The barbed stinger gets stuck in skin and tears away from the bee.

questions.q: Which insects make light to attract mates?
questions.fact: The light from fireflies makes almost no heat.

questions.q: How do crickets make their chirping sound?
questions.fact: You can roughly estimate the temperature by counting cricket chirps.

questions.q: Which insect is famous for carrying many times its own body weight?
questions.fact: Some ants can lift around 50 times their own weight.

questions.q: Which insect is known for spending years underground and then all coming out together to sing loudly?
questions.fact: Some periodical cicadas stay underground for 17 years.

questions.q: Which insect only drinks blood when it is a female?
questions.fact: Female mosquitoes need protein from blood to make their eggs, while males drink plant nectar.

questions.q: Which animal kills more people each year than any other wild animal?
questions.fact: Mosquitoes spread diseases like malaria.

questions.q: Which insect has been around since before the dinosaurs and can hunt other insects in mid-air?
questions.fact: Dragonflies catch a very high share of the prey they chase.

questions.q: Which beetle is red with black spots and eats aphids?
questions.fact: One ladybug can eat thousands of aphids during its life.

questions.q: Which insect can hide by looking just like a twig?
questions.fact: Some stick insects are longer than a ruler.

questions.q: What do dung beetles do with animal poop?
choices: Roll it into balls and eat it or lay eggs in it
questions.fact: Some dung beetles use the Milky Way in the night sky to find their way.

questions.q: Which insect group has the most species on Earth?
questions.fact: Scientists have described about 400,000 kinds of beetles.

questions.q: What do termites mainly eat?
questions.fact: Some African termites build mounds taller than a grown-up.

questions.q: What is the young of a dragonfly that lives underwater called?
questions.fact: A dragonfly nymph can spend years underwater before becoming a flying adult.

questions.q: How does a spider catch most of its food?
choices: In silk webs or by hunting
questions.fact: Weight for weight, spider silk can be stronger than steel.

questions.q: Which spider is famous for eating its mate?
questions.fact: Female black widows do sometimes eat males, but not every time.

questions.q: Which spider is large and hairy and sometimes kept as a pet?
questions.fact: Some tarantulas can live for more than 20 years.

questions.q: Which spider mother carries her babies on her back?
questions.fact: Hundreds of tiny spiderlings may ride on their mother's back.

questions.q: Which ape is the closest living relative of humans, along with the bonobo?
questions.fact: Humans and chimpanzees share about 98 percent of their DNA.

questions.q: Which is the largest ape?
questions.fact: A big male gorilla, called a silverback, can weigh more than 180 kilograms.

questions.q: Which ape has reddish-orange hair and lives in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra?
questions.fact: Orangutan means person of the forest in the Malay language.

questions.q: Which apes swing through the trees with super long arms and sing loud songs?
questions.fact: Gibbons can swing between branches at up to about 55 kilometers per hour.

questions.q: Which scientist became famous for studying wild chimpanzees in Tanzania?
questions.fact: Jane Goodall discovered that chimpanzees make and use tools.

questions.q: Where do wild lemurs live?
questions.fact: Lemurs live naturally only on the island of Madagascar and a few small nearby islands.

questions.q: What is the difference between a monkey and an ape?
choices: Apes have tails and monkeys do not
Most monkeys have tails and apes do not
questions.fact: Gorillas, chimpanzees, orangutans and gibbons are all apes.

questions.q: Which monkey is known as one of the loudest land animals?
questions.fact: A howler monkey's call can be heard several kilometers away through the forest.

questions.q: Which monkey lives in snowy mountains in Japan and bathes in hot springs?
questions.fact: These monkeys are often called snow monkeys.

questions.q: Which monkey has a bright red and blue face?
questions.fact: Mandrills are the largest monkeys in the world.

questions.q: What is the largest rodent in the world?
questions.fact: Capybaras live in South America and love to swim.

questions.q: Which rodent stores food in big cheek pouches?
questions.fact: A hamster can stuff its cheek pouches until its head looks twice as wide.

questions.q: Is a rabbit a rodent?
choices: It is a type of cat
questions.fact: Rabbits have a second small pair of upper front teeth behind the first pair.

questions.q: Which pet rodent comes from South America and makes squeaking sounds called wheeking?
questions.fact: Guinea pigs are not pigs and do not come from Guinea.

questions.q: Which animal has the softest, thickest fur of any land animal?
questions.fact: A chinchilla can grow about 60 hairs from a single hair follicle.

questions.q: Which small mammal digs tunnels and is almost blind?
questions.fact: A mole can dig about 18 meters of tunnel in a day.

questions.q: Which African rodent has almost no hair and lives in colonies with a queen, like bees?
questions.fact: Naked mole-rats can live more than 30 years, a very long time for a rodent.

questions.q: How do most bats find insects in the dark?
questions.fact: Bats send out high-pitched calls and listen for the echoes.

questions.q: What do vampire bats drink?
questions.fact: Vampire bats share blood meals with roost mates who did not find food.

questions.q: Which bat is the largest, with wings over 1.5 meters wide?
questions.fact: Flying foxes eat fruit and nectar, not insects.

questions.q: How do most bats rest?
questions.fact: Bats have special tendons that lock their toes, so hanging takes no effort.

questions.q: Which animal is the slowest mammal in the world?
questions.fact: Sloths move so slowly that tiny algae grow in their fur, giving them a greenish tint.

questions.q: Which animal sleeps through winter in a deep, long sleep?
questions.fact: This long winter sleep is called hibernation.

questions.q: What is it called when an animal travels a long way each year to find food or warmth?
questions.fact: Some caribou herds migrate thousands of kilometers each year.

questions.q: What is it called when an animal's colors help it blend into its surroundings?
questions.fact: Arctic foxes turn white in winter and brown in summer to stay hidden.

questions.q: What do we call animals that are active mostly at night?
questions.fact: Owls, bats and raccoons are all nocturnal.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that eats both plants and meat?
questions.fact: Bears, pigs and most people are omnivores.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that eats only meat?
questions.fact: Cats are true carnivores and must eat meat to stay healthy.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that hunts other animals for food?
questions.fact: The animals that predators hunt are called prey.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that eats dead animals it did not kill?
questions.fact: Vultures are important scavengers that help clean up nature.

questions.q: What is a living thing that lives on or in another and harms it called?
questions.fact: Fleas, ticks and tapeworms are all parasites.

questions.q: What is the place where an animal naturally lives called?
questions.fact: A habitat gives an animal food, water, shelter and space.

questions.q: What do we call a type of animal that has completely died out?
questions.fact: Once an animal is extinct, it is gone forever.

questions.q: Which flightless bird from the island of Mauritius went extinct in the 1600s?
questions.fact: The phrase dead as a dodo comes from this bird.

questions.q: Which huge, hairy relative of elephants lived during the Ice Age?

questions.fact: The last known passenger pigeon, named Martha, died at the Cincinnati Zoo.

questions.fact: The last known Tasmanian tiger, also called a thylacine, died in a zoo in 1936.

questions.fact: Stegosaurus had a brain about the size of a walnut, tiny for such a big body.

questions.q: What does the word dinosaur mean?

questions.q: Which long-necked dinosaur is one of the longest animals ever?

questions.q: What kind of animal is a seahorse?

questions.q: What kind of animal is a whale shark?

questions.q: What kind of animal is a bat?
questions.fact: Bat mothers feed their babies milk, like all mammals.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a penguin?

questions.q: What kind of animal is a salamander?

questions.q: What kind of animal is a jellyfish?

questions.q: What are animals with backbones called?

questions.q: What is a baby butterfly or moth called?

questions.q: What is the only continent where no ants live naturally?

questions.q: What do camels store in their humps?

questions.q: How many humps does a dromedary camel have?
questions.fact: Bactrian camels have two humps, and dromedaries have one.

questions.q: Which South American animal is related to the camel and often used to carry loads in the Andes?

questions.q: Which animal from the Himalayas has long shaggy hair and is used to carry loads at high altitudes?
questions.fact: Yaks have extra-large lungs and hearts to help them live where the air is thin.

questions.q: Which animal is the national animal of Scotland?

questions.q: Which animal lived on the Great Plains of North America in herds of millions?

questions.q: Which is the largest kind of deer?

questions.q: In which kind of deer do both males and females grow antlers?
questions.fact: Reindeer are called caribou in North America.

questions.q: What are horns on cattle, goats and sheep covered in?
questions.fact: Unlike antlers, true horns are not shed and keep growing.

questions.q: What is a rhinoceros horn made of?

questions.q: Which animal has the thickest fur of any marine mammal?
questions.fact: A sea otter has about a million hairs in every square inch of skin.

questions.q: What color is a polar bear's skin?

questions.q: Which bear is the largest meat-eating land mammal?

questions.q: Which bear has a hump on its shoulders made of muscle?

questions.q: Where do wild giant pandas live?

questions.q: What is special about a giant panda's wrist?

It has an extra bone that works like a thumb

questions.q: Which African animal has black and white striped fur?

questions.q: Which animal looks like a mix of a zebra and a giraffe but is related to the giraffe?

questions.q: How long is a giraffe's tongue?

questions.q: How many neck bones does a giraffe have?

questions.q: Which animal is famous for curling into a spiky ball?

questions.q: Which animal is covered in scales and is one of the most trafficked mammals in the world?

questions.q: Which animal eats ants and termites with a very long sticky tongue but has no teeth?
questions.fact: A giant anteater's tongue can flick in and out about 150 times a minute.

questions.q: Which animal's name comes from an Afrikaans word meaning earth pig?
questions.fact: Aardvarks dig burrows that many other animals later use as homes.

questions.q: Which small African mammal stands on its back legs to keep watch?
questions.fact: Meerkats take turns as sentries, calling out warnings when danger comes.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for being stubborn and is a relative of the horse?

questions.q: What is a mule?

questions.q: Which horse breed is often known as the fastest for short sprints?
questions.fact: Quarter horses got their name from racing a quarter mile.

questions.q: How do horses usually sleep?

questions.q: Which farm animal has a stomach with four parts?

questions.q: Which farm animal is known for being very smart and learning tricks quickly?

questions.q: Why do pigs roll in mud?

questions.q: Which bird lays the eggs that most people eat?

questions.q: What is the fleshy red part on top of a chicken's head called?

questions.q: What is wool mostly from?
questions.fact: A sheep that is never sheared will keep growing more and more wool.

questions.q: Which pet animal is descended from wolves?

questions.q: Which dog breed is known as the fastest?

questions.q: Which dog breed was bred to hunt badgers and has a long body and short legs?
questions.fact: Dachshund means badger dog in German.

questions.q: Which is the smallest dog breed?
questions.fact: Chihuahuas are named after a state in Mexico.

questions.q: Which dog breed often works as a rescue dog in the Swiss Alps?
questions.fact: Saint Bernards are famous in stories for carrying small barrels, but that is mostly a myth.

questions.q: Which dog breed has spots and was once used to run beside horse-drawn fire carts?
questions.fact: Dalmatian puppies are born pure white and get their spots as they grow.

questions.q: Which dog breed is famous for pulling sleds in cold places?
questions.fact: Some huskies have one blue eye and one brown eye.

questions.q: How does a dog cool itself down?
questions.fact: Dogs only have a few sweat glands, mostly in their paw pads.

questions.q: How good is a dog's sense of smell compared to a person's?
questions.fact: Dogs can be trained to sniff out lost people, bombs and even some illnesses.

questions.q: Why do cats purr?
choices: Often when happy, but also to calm themselves

questions.q: What are a cat's whiskers mainly used for?
choices: Feeling their way and sensing things nearby

questions.q: Which animal can see colors humans cannot, like ultraviolet light?

No, they can remember for months

questions.q: Which tiny animal can survive outer space, boiling and freezing?

questions.fact: Giraffes sleep only a few hours a day in total.

questions.q: Which animal's heart beats only a few times a minute when it dives deep?

questions.q: What is the name of the colorful flap of skin that helps a male frigatebird attract a mate?

questions.q: Which long-legged bird wades in shallow water and spears fish with its sharp beak?

questions.q: Which large, flightless parrot from New Zealand is critically endangered?

questions.q: What color are a robin's eggs?

questions.q: Which huge deep-sea animal was first photographed alive in the wild in 2004?

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Sn?

questions.q: About how many known elements are there, as of 2025?

questions.q: What are the particles with a positive charge in an atom's nucleus?
questions.fact: The number of protons decides which element an atom is.

questions.q: What particles in an atom's nucleus have no electric charge?
questions.fact: Neutrons were discovered in 1932 by James Chadwick.

questions.q: What is the atomic number of an element?

questions.q: What is a molecule?

questions.fact: You breathe out carbon dioxide every time you exhale.

questions.q: What is rust?
